title: Lyra escalation postmortem follow-up
header:
Date: 2027-01-18 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 54m
Attendees: Sofia Nguyen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Redwood CSM), Daniel Park (Lyra VP Eng), Maya Ortiz (Lyra SRE), Amir Khan (Lyra Security)
summary: Follow-up on the Jan 14 outage: confirmed root cause as KV cache eviction thrashing plus a memory leak in the batcher goroutine leading to elevated 5xx and latency spikes. Hotfix and rollback reduced errors; agreed on audit plan, improved canary traffic, and customer communications including SLA credit proposal.
action_items: Marcus Lee - implement and verify root-cause patch to batcher (memory leak / eviction) - due 2027-01-22
Priya Raman - draft and send customer-facing postmortem and SLA credit proposal - due 2027-01-19
Sofia Nguyen - coordinate exec update and confirm credit amount with finance - due 2027-01-21
Maya Ortiz (Lyra) - provide additional request traces and logs for the 02:15-03:00 UTC window on 2027-01-14 - due 2027-01-20
next_steps: Share final postmortem doc with timeline and root cause by 2027-01-20
Schedule dedicated load test and runbook dry-run in Lyra test org by 2027-01-24
Deploy canary of patched batcher for 48h with enhanced tracing, then roll to production if stable
Review SLO and auto-scaling thresholds and add healthcheck for KV cache pressure metric
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Nguyen: Okay everyone, thanks for jumping on. This is our follow-up for the Lyra escalation, Jan 14 outage. Quick run through agenda - Marcus will walk root cause, then Priya on customer comms, then next steps.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Yeah hi. So quick TL;DR - we traced the elevated 5xx and latency spikes to the batcher path where the KV cache eviction policy was thrashing under a specific request distribution from Lyra's workload. There was also a memory leak in the batching goroutine that exacerbated the pressure.
[00:35] Daniel Park: Just to be clear, we saw requests queuing up and then a spike to about 30% error rates for ~40 minutes, correct?
[00:42] Marcus Lee: Correct, on the affected model routes. The sequence length distribution plus a burst of long streaming sessions caused a lot of prefix cache churn; eviction triggered reclamation that incorrectly freed items still referenced by live KV handles - leading to panics and 503s. Also our autoscaler didn't kick in fast enough because the cache pressure metric was under-weighted.
[01:05] Maya Ortiz: And we did get a lot of timeouts on our side; some of our downstream job processors flagged retries. We pulled logs, there are a few hundred unique trace ids showing the same stack.
[01:20] Amir Khan: From security side, any data exposure concerns with the eviction bug?
[01:26] Marcus Lee: We assessed that it's a memory management bug, not an IO leak. No evidence of data exfiltration - KMS and disk encryption remained intact. We'll include the full forensics in the postmortem doc.
[01:40] Sofia Nguyen: Walk us through mitigations that were applied in the incident window.
[01:45] Marcus Lee: At 02:23 UTC we rolled back a recent micro-optimization to the batcher code that reduced locking; rollback immediately reduced panics, but latency still high. Then at 03:05 we pushed a hotfix that changes eviction thresholds and adds a guard to the KV handle lifecycle. That reduced error rates to baseline by ~03:30. We also increased the autoscaling headroom temporarily.
[02:10] Daniel Park: The rollback helped quickly, appreciate that. Why didn't the canary catch it?
[02:15] Marcus Lee: The canary config was using a smaller sequence length distribution and lower concurrency; it didn't mirror Lyra's production traffic pattern. We're updating canary generation to better reflect customer's traffic, including synthetic long-stream sessions.
[02:33] Priya Raman: On comms - Lyra's customer ops had a lot of incoming escalations. We proposed a statement with timeline, impact, root cause and mitigations; also suggested a service credit. Daniel - is the proposed credit okay?
[02:48] Daniel Park: The proposed credit looks reasonable, we just want to confirm the threshold calculations.
[02:53] Sofia Nguyen: We'll include the math in the postmortem. Priya will own the customer note.
[03:00] Marcus Lee: Longer-term fixes: 1) full memory safety audit of the batcher and KV code paths, 2) expose a new metric for KV cache pressure and add an automated healthcheck that triggers autoscaler earlier, 3) more conservative eviction policy defaults for Dedicated customers, and 4) better canary traffic generation for long streams.
[03:28] Maya Ortiz: For the audit, can we get a timeline? We need to know when this is closed so we can decide on re-architecting some of our clients.
[03:36] Marcus Lee: We're estimating a 3-week engineering work cycle for audit and mitigations before we can call it fully remediated. We'll provide incremental PRs and evidence.
[03:45] Amir Khan: Also want to record that from Lyra security they'll want SOC2 control evidence and the code diff for the patch; we can share limited diffs under NDA if needed.
[03:56] Sofia Nguyen: Noted. We'll coordinate with legal and security to share the right artifacts.
[04:04] Daniel Park: A couple of asks - first, can Redwood run the load test against a provisioned Dedicated test cluster with our traffic shape? Second, can we get an SLA credit reconciliation spreadsheet?
[04:15] Sofia Nguyen: Yes to both. We'll provision a test cluster and run the test jointly; Marcus and Priya will own scheduling. Priya - you'll take the spreadsheet and the customer note.
[04:26] Priya Raman: Yep I can do that, will send draft by tomorrow.
[04:30] Marcus Lee: One operational note - we're also adding more verbose tracing for the batcher path (request id, kv-handle id) for 14 days post-deploy to validate the fix in production. We'll sample aggressively for Lyra routes to be safe.
[04:47] Maya Ortiz: Good. Also can we get a runbook update so our on-call knows mitigation steps?
[04:52] Marcus Lee: Absolutely - I will update the runbook and add explicit checks for KV pressure and steps to rollback or increase autoscaler headroom.
[05:00] Sofia Nguyen: Ok wrapping - recap of action items and owners, send postmortem and credit proposal, schedule load test, patch verification and runbook updates. Any other questions?
[05:12] Daniel Park: No, thanks. Appreciate the quick turnaround and detail.
[05:18] Sofia Nguyen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up on due dates in the action items.
[05:25] [meeting ends]
notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors in auto transcript; summary cleaned. Customer requested SOC2 evidence and code diff under NDA. Finance will review SLA credit proposal.
